Combine all author's author_pfas_d# into one author_pfas
```{r}
author_pfas_d1 <- rownames_to_column(author_pfas_d1, var="gene")
author_pfas_d4 <- rownames_to_column(author_pfas_d4, var="gene")
author_pfas_d10 <- rownames_to_column(author_pfas_d10, var = "gene")
author_pfas_d14 <- rownames_to_column(author_pfas_d14, var="gene")

add_dur <- function(df, d) {
  i <- colnames(df) != "gene"
  colnames(df)[i] <- paste0(colnames(df)[i], "_d", d)
  df
}

author_pfas <- add_dur(author_pfas_d1, 1) %>%
  full_join(add_dur(author_pfas_d4, 4),   by = "gene") %>%
  full_join(add_dur(author_pfas_d10, 10), by = "gene") %>%
  full_join(add_dur(author_pfas_d14, 14), by = "gene") %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = "gene")

tail(author_pfas)
colnames(author_pfas)
# for some reason, the sample titles have duplicates and are not all unique across all durations, so .x was added in full_join
```

Add a new column to unified_index to match pfas sample names of authors with the unified naming index
```{r}
is_pfas <- grepl("_R1_001$", unified_index$title)

title_dose <- sub("^[A-Za-z]+([0-9.]+)(?:D[0-9.]+)?_.*$", "\\1", unified_index$title, perl = TRUE)

dose_key <- gsub("-", ".", as.character(unified_index$dose))

# check what the dose things look like from author sample names vs my pipeline index
unique(dose_key)
unique(unified_index$dose)

dmso <- is_pfas & unified_index$chemical == "DMSO"

# authors’ names the DMSO dose is not always 0, as seen in unified_index$title vs $dose
# therefore, we use the title to get the dose to make the author's style of sample naming
dose_key[dmso] <- gsub("-", ".",
  as.character(round(as.numeric(title_dose[dmso]) / 1000, 10)))

unified_index$author_key_pfas <- ifelse(
  is_pfas,
  paste0(unified_index$chemical, "_", dose_key, "_",
         sub("^[^_]+_(\\d+)_.*$", "\\1", unified_index$title),
         "_d", unified_index$duration),
  NA
)
```

Rename bowtie_pfas with the unified titles
```{r}

# CAN only confirm with Ref right now with exact match. But can test with PFAS to see if samples correlate

#Choose which samples of specific dose and duration you want to look at
target_metadata <- unified_index %>%
  # filter(chemical == "DMSO", duration == 1, dose == 0)
  filter(chemical == filter_chemical, duration == filter_duration, dose == filter_dose)


# 2. Find which sample_id from your metadata actually exist in the count matrix columns
common_srrs <- intersect(target_metadata$X, colnames(bowtie_pfas))
# YOU SWITCH OUT BOWTIE REF HERE WITH WHAT     DATASET     YOU WANT TO COMPARE

# 3. Subset the count matrix using those valid SRRs
bowtie_pfas_filtered <- bowtie_pfas[, common_srrs]

# 4. Align the metadata to match the exact column order of the filtered count matrix
matched_bowtie_meta <- target_metadata[match(colnames(bowtie_pfas_filtered),
                                                target_metadata$X), ]

# 5. Safely assign the clean sample IDs as column names
colnames(bowtie_pfas_filtered) <- matched_bowtie_meta$X
```

Rename author_pfas with the unified titles
```{r}
# 1. Filter your unified index metadata for the specific conditions you want (e.g., DMSO, duration 1, dose 0)
# target_metadata <- unified_index %>%
#   filter(chemical == "DMSO", duration == 1, dose == 0)

# 2. Find which author columns match the tsv_title in your filtered metadata
common_author_cols <- intersect(colnames(author_pfas), target_metadata$author_key_pfas)
author_pfas_filtered <- author_pfas[, common_author_cols]

# 3. Match the metadata rows to the current column order of author_pfas_filtered
matched_author_meta <- target_metadata[match(colnames(author_pfas_filtered), target_metadata$author_key_pfas), ]

# 4. Construct the new unified sample names incorporating duration, dose, AND keeping "pool" (title/GSM)
author_sample_id <- make.unique(
  paste(
    gsub(" ", "_", matched_author_meta$chemical),
    paste0(matched_author_meta$duration, "d"),
    paste0(matched_author_meta$dose, "uM"),
    # matched_author_meta$title, # Keeps the pool/sample identifier (e.g., pool1_S1)
    sub("^[^_]+_(\\d+)_.*$", "\\1", matched_author_meta$title),
    paste0("author"),
    sep = "-"
  ),
  sep = "-"
)

# 5. Assign the new descriptive sample IDs to the filtered author count matrix
colnames(author_pfas_filtered) <- author_sample_id
```

# only PFAS
Creating the heatmap to compare author_pfas and bowtie_pfas
```{r}

# 1. Combine your two count matrices (e.g., author_pfas and bowtie_pfas) by gene rows
# Ensure they share the exact same genes using a full_join or matching row names:
common_genes <- intersect(rownames(author_pfas_filtered), rownames(bowtie_pfas_filtered))

combined_counts <- cbind(
  author_pfas_filtered[common_genes, ],
  bowtie_pfas_filtered[common_genes, ]
)

# Optional: Log-transform or variance-stabilize counts first for better distance metrics (e.g., log2(counts + 1))
log_counts <- log2(as.matrix(combined_counts) + 1)



# # 2. Transpose so samples are rows, then compute Euclidean distance between samples
# sample_dists <- dist(t(log_counts), method = "euclidean")
# sample_dist_matrix <- as.matrix(sample_dists)


# 2
# Pearson correlation between samples (columns)
sample_cor_matrix <- cor(log_counts, method = "pearson")
# sample_cor_matrix <- cor(log_counts, method = "spearman")
# Convert to a distance: 1 - r
sample_dists <- as.dist(1 - sample_cor_matrix)




# 1. Create an annotation data frame matching the columns of your combined matrix
# Ensure the row names of this annotation data frame match the column names of your sample_dist_matrix
annotation_df = data.frame(
  Pipeline = ifelse(grepl("author", colnames(sample_cor_matrix), ignore.case = TRUE), "Author", "Bowtie"), # if has pool=author
  row.names = colnames(sample_cor_matrix)
)

# 3. Plot the sample-to-sample distance heatmap
pheatmap(
  # sample_dist_matrix,
  sample_cor_matrix,
  clustering_distance_rows = sample_dists,
  clustering_distance_cols = sample_dists,
  annotation_row = annotation_df,
  annotation_col = annotation_df,
  fontsize_row = 5,        # Adjust row font size (try 5 or 6)
  fontsize_col = 6,        # Adjust column font size (try 5 or 6)
  angle_col = "45",        # Tilts the bottom column labels so they don't crash into each other
  # main = "Sample Distance Heatmap (Euclidean)"
  main = "Sample Distance Heatmap (Pearson)"
)
```

Spearman correlation heatmap, instead of pearson (ranking based, look at ranking of genes per sample, instead of measuring covariance between samples)
Creating the heatmap to compare author_pfas and bowtie_pfas
```{r}

# 1. Combine your two count matrices (e.g., author_pfas and bowtie_pfas) by gene rows
# Ensure they share the exact same genes using a full_join or matching row names:
common_genes <- intersect(rownames(author_pfas_filtered), rownames(bowtie_pfas_filtered))

combined_counts <- cbind(
  author_pfas_filtered[common_genes, ],
  bowtie_pfas_filtered[common_genes, ]
)

# Optional: Log-transform or variance-stabilize counts first for better distance metrics (e.g., log2(counts + 1))
log_counts <- log2(as.matrix(combined_counts) + 1)



# # 2. Transpose so samples are rows, then compute Euclidean distance between samples
# sample_dists <- dist(t(log_counts), method = "euclidean")
# sample_dist_matrix <- as.matrix(sample_dists)


# 2
# Pearson correlation between samples (columns)
# sample_cor_matrix <- cor(log_counts, method = "pearson")
sample_cor_matrix <- cor(log_counts, method = "spearman")
# Convert to a distance: 1 - r
sample_dists <- as.dist(1 - sample_cor_matrix)




# 1. Create an annotation data frame matching the columns of your combined matrix
# Ensure the row names of this annotation data frame match the column names of your sample_dist_matrix
annotation_df = data.frame(
  Pipeline = ifelse(grepl("author", colnames(sample_cor_matrix), ignore.case = TRUE), "Author", "Bowtie"), # if has pool=author
  row.names = colnames(sample_cor_matrix)
)

# 3. Plot the sample-to-sample distance heatmap
pheatmap(
  # sample_dist_matrix,
  sample_cor_matrix,
  clustering_distance_rows = sample_dists,
  clustering_distance_cols = sample_dists,
  annotation_row = annotation_df,
  annotation_col = annotation_df,
  fontsize_row = 5,        # Adjust row font size (try 5 or 6)
  fontsize_col = 6,        # Adjust column font size (try 5 or 6)
  angle_col = "45",        # Tilts the bottom column labels so they don't crash into each other
  # main = "Sample Distance Heatmap (Euclidean)"
  main = "Sample Distance Heatmap (Spearman)"
)
```
